mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.25% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent higher borrowing costs compressing equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day moving average during the same period (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment months) above 150,000 coinciding with a rising UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4%, predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market expansion supports corporate optimism.
regime_hint: expanding labor market with low unemployment
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day moving average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in HOUST (residential construction) of at least 2% for three consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak housing demand reduces equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly < previous month for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 70% of such events (empirical frequency).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) grows at a monthly rate exceeding 2% for two consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to stronger supply-side momentum boosting equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly growth > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 10-day moving average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of over 0.5% in a single month followed by a sustained FEDFUNDS rate below 4% predicts a positive S&P 60-day forward return as inflation fears recede and rates stay accommodative.
regime_hint: transitional to lower inflation with loose policy
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly PAYEMS reading above 160,000 in a regime where UNRATE is below 4% predicts a positive 20-day forward return as strong labor demand supports corporate earnings growth.
regime_hint: labor market expansion with low unemployment
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive in 80% of such events (frequency test).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in GDPC1 (GDP) of over 1% signals a demand contraction, which is associated with a negative S&P 5-day forward return as market anticipates weaker economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly < previous month for 2 months AND change > -1%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative in 90% of such events (backtest frequency).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3.5% for three consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to reduced labor market friction and stronger supply-side conditions.
regime_hint: low unemployment and easing labor market pressures
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive in 60% of such regimes (empirical failure rate).
